title: RLogic: Recursive Logical Rule Learning from Knowledge Graphs

problem.claim: The work addresses automatic learning of logical rules from knowledge graphs.

gap.claim: Existing methods largely rely on observed rule instances for rule evaluation, limiting generalization and causing severe computational inefficiency.

contributions.claim: RLogic uses a predicate-representation-learning-based scoring model trained on sampled rule instances.
RLogic incorporates the deductive nature of logical rules into rule learning, including when rules lack supporting evidence.
RLogic recursively decomposes a large sequential model into smaller atomic models to support deeper deductive reasoning.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show RLogic is superior to existing state-of-the-art algorithms in efficiency and effectiveness.

narrative_sequence.summary: Logical rules support domain knowledge representation and symbolic reasoning-based intelligence.
Integrating logical rules into learning tasks can improve label-efficient learning, while automatic rule learning from knowledge graphs remains important.
Existing rule-evaluation methods depend heavily on observed rule instances and consequently have generalization and efficiency problems.
RLogic combines learned predicate-based scoring, deductive reasoning, and recursive decomposition into atomic models.
The authors report improved efficiency and effectiveness over existing state-of-the-art algorithms.

source_observation.claim: Rule evaluation can be based on learned predicate representations trained from sampled instances rather than complete reliance on observed rule instances.

interpretation.claim: A learned representation may reduce dependence on direct evidence coverage and improve scalability.

application.claim: For rule-learning systems facing sparse evidence or high evaluation cost, consider representation-based scoring with sampled training instances.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish when sampled-instance training preserves accuracy or how it behaves outside the reported experiments.

source_observation.claim: RLogic integrates deductive reasoning and recursively decomposes sequential models into atomic models.

interpretation.claim: Explicitly modeling deductive structure and decomposing complex reasoning may support deeper rule inference.

application.claim: When reasoning depth or rule support is limited, consider architectures that encode deduction and break complex inference into smaller recursive units.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the recursion limits, failure modes, or computational trade-offs of the decomposition.

unknowns: Datasets, baselines, metrics, and experimental settings are unspecified.
The abstract does not quantify efficiency or effectiveness improvements.
The specific scoring architecture, sampling procedure, and recursive training details are unspecified.
